_meta.do_not_hand_edit: This file is GENERATED ground truth extracted from Stata's own scheme and style files. Regenerate it by re-running scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py; do not hand-edit.
_meta.lineplot_vs_line: Stata keeps two per-plot line stubs apart: 'p#line' is the connecting line of twoway connected, while 'p#lineplot' is the line twoway line itself draws. They are NOT interchangeable: under s2mono, 'linepattern p#line' resolves to the inherited 'linepattern p solid' while 'linepattern p#lineplot' is solid/dash/vshortdash/..., so three overlaid twoway line plots are drawn with three different dashes. Only the s2mono branch (s2mono, stmono2, stsj, sj) declares any lineplot key; for every other scheme p_lineplot_* is the p#stub->pstub->p#->p fallback result, not something the scheme wrote. 'lineplot_declared' records which case a scheme is in, per class, so a translation can tell an inherited value from a declared one instead of presenting the two alike. The indirection is in Stata's own style files: style/seriesstyle-p#line.style points a line plot's line at linestyle p#line, and style/linestyle-p#line.style then sets width/color/pattern from 'scheme p#lineplot' -- whereas style/linestyle-p#.style (the connected-plot linestyle) sets color/pattern from 'scheme p#line'. Stata documents the three keys in scheme_line_plots.sthlp, and scheme_line_plots.sthlp plus scheme_shared_plots.sthlp give the fallback: a scheme without the line-plot-specific entries uses the entries shared among all plottypes, namely 'color p#' and 'linepattern p' -- NOT 'linepattern p#line', which is a different stub.
_meta.intensity_multiplier_rule: f<=1: c' = round(255-(255-c)*f); f>1: c' = round(c/f); clamp [0,255]; round half away from zero. Verified empirically against Stata 19.5 SVG export over 24 colour/multiplier cases.
_meta.color_none: Stata colour 'none' is emitted as JSON null.
_meta.sources: Per-scheme 'sources' records, for every extracted property, the exact '<class> <key>' directive that supplied the value after the #include chain and the p#stub->pstub->p#->p fallback were applied. '<class-default>' means the value came from a bare two-token class default line (e.g. 'intensity full'), not from a named key. Notably no Stata base scheme sets 'intensity area', so area_alpha always resolves to the intensity class default.

units.*_size.value: Stata relative size units (sztype gives the kind); pt_at_4in is that value in points on Stata's 4-inch reference graph
units.default_line_width/grid_line_width.value: Stata linewidth units, the same relative size; pt_at_4in likewise
units.*_alpha.pct: percent as written in the scheme; alpha = pct/100

relative_size.definition: help size: 'relative size, where size 100 = minimum of width and height of graph'; every official gsize-/symbolsize-*.style sets sztype relative, and linewidthstyle's numeric form is the same unit
relative_size.formula_pt: pt = value / 100 * min(graphsize x, graphsize y) [inches] * 72
relative_size.note: pt_at_4in figures use Stata's 4-inch reference (s2color is 5.5 x 4in); at a scheme's own graphsize multiply by min(x, y) / 4

gsize.dash_rule: a numeric gsize is pt = value * 2.88 (the 4-inch reference), written f'{pt:g}pt' with no minimum and no truncation; a keyword takes its pt_at_4in below

symbolsize.dash_rule: a keyword takes its pt_at_4in below; a numeric symbolsize is pt = value * 2.88; pixels anchor medium (4.4pt) at 8px, i.e. px = pt * 8 / 4.4
symbolsize.not_the_gsize_ladder: large/medium = 1.59 here vs 1.27 for gsize; small/medium = 0.68 vs 0.73

linewidth.dash_rule: a numeric linewidth is px = value * 5.0 (medium .30 anchored at dash's 1.5px); keywords still go through OptionTranslator._LWIDTH_MAP, whose ratios are not this ladder's -- recorded as a follow-up

_meta.grid_switches: draw_major_hgrid/draw_minor_hgrid (x axis, the vertical lines at the x ticks) and draw_major_vgrid/draw_minor_vgrid (y axis, the horizontal lines) are EFFECTIVE values: twoway builds the x axis with axisstyle horizontal_default and the y axis with axisstyle vertical_default, the scheme maps each role to a style name, and style/axisstyle-<name>.style names the yesno key that is read. Per-scheme 'grid_axes' records that chain and 'sources' the key that supplied each value (economist's y axis: draw_major_nlt_vgrid / draw_minor_nlt_vgrid via vertical_nolinetick). draw_major_grid/draw_minor_grid are the bare keys as transcribed; no style file reads them.

note().note: Stata's note textbox does not read gsize note

textbox_styles.source: style/textboxstyle-<name>.style: set size scheme <name>; set color scheme <name>
